scope: R-008/A: when does the display window become unreachable, measured inside the stage checkpoint
question: is the display domain already down when XBL hands over, or is it turned off later by our own dispatch
method: two read-only loads of 0x0ae6b800 and 0x0ae6c000 placed inside the EnumaStageCheckpoint branch, which the delay-control experiment proved executes and honours the configured delay

trials.purpose: execution proof: an unmapped address must hang if the read really runs

conclusion: B hanging proves the read really executes, so A returning cleanly proves the display window was still reachable at that point. The domain is therefore NOT already down at handover: it is turned off later, during our own dispatch.
replaces: the earlier working hypothesis that XBL tears the display down on EnterFastbootExit and leaves the domain down. The bus-hang mechanism itself still holds (reading a window whose clocks are off hangs the bus, as the Qualcomm bus-hang example shows), but the cause of the clocks being off is now internal to this firmware.
consequences: no OEM protocol providers need to be added and no MMCX or RPMh sequence has to be written: the domain is already up when we take over
the fix direction becomes either reading the window before dispatch, or identifying which driver in the dispatch turns the clocks off

the 23 earlier steps read the window during or after dispatch, so their values were taken while the clocks were being removed; their evidence grade stays unknown, and the mechanism behind that is now explained rather than mysterious
the historical intermittent successes are consistent with a read that happened to land before the teardown
next: bisect with the same pair of loads at stage 11, which sits right after CoreDispatcher returns: a clean stage 10 plus a stalled stage 11 localises the teardown to the dispatch itself
interpretation: A与B两笔对照闭合:死地址挂死证明读确实执行,故A的正常返回证明显示窗口在stage10仍可访问;teardown发生在本固件派发期间而非XBL跳转瞬间。推翻了此前'XBL关闭显示'的解释,但保留unclocked access致挂的机制。不需要补驱动或自写上电序列,方向改为在派发前读取或定位关闭者。
